analysis.title: US Growth & Inflation Recap, BoJ on Hold, EUR Too Low, and Canada Has to Deliver
key_insights: UBS sales desk says US growth is robust across most dimensions except real estate/housing. Cyclical survey indicators point to hot nominal growth, labor market signals point to cooling but not cracking, and personal consumption is robust even though income growth lags spending.

UBS expects headline and core US inflation to move lower in 1Q27 and 2Q27. Core goods inflation should stop contributing to higher readings, energy base effects will contribute to the decline, and inflation expectations are well contained, with 5y5y inflation swaps in a comfortable range.
Recent equity stress has led the equal weight index to outperform the market cap weighted index on a YTD basis.

EURUSD reversed during the ECB press conference after spot flirted with new one-year lows. The author finds it increasingly unlikely that EUR falls below 1.11 or stays there near-term, and expects spot to converge toward macro-implied fair value.

The author's support for EUR cites higher FY27 eurozone GDP estimates (almost back to pre-US-Iran conflict levels), stable ERZ7 pricing at about 3 implied hikes versus more than 4 for SFIZ7, OAT stress off local peaks, and improving option-implied positioning. The author says they are not a EUR bull.
Long EURUSD was added to the UBS systematic portfolio on 10/27 and will be discussed further in the upcoming weekly FX Divergence.

The BoJ left rates unchanged at 1.25% in an 8-to-1 vote. Market-implied pricing for a December hike is about 21bps, but JPY 1y1y has come off its highs with almost a full 25bps of implied hikes removed.
USDJPY is trading in the 157 range and 1m realized volatility has fallen below 6 vols.

Canada August monthly GDP is due with an average analyst estimate of +20bps m/m, which would put y/y at +1.64%. That would be the highest y/y reading outside June's 2.1%. The author says a solid path of m/m growth is integral given the Bank of Canada's rosy growth outlook for consumption and fixed investment.
USDCAD spot at 1.3950 reflects implied spot fair value, so the author sees less asymmetry in initiating longs.
